senses.gloss: The part of a vehicle's engine cooling system that lets heat escape.
examples: Steam poured out of the *radiator*, so we pulled over.
The mechanic found a slow leak in the *radiator*.
Older *radiators* need a mix of coolant and water.

senses.gloss: A rude noise made by sticking out the tongue and blowing.
examples: The toddler blew a *raspberry* at his sister and giggled.
Fans blew *raspberries* when the umpire called him out.
She answered my question with a loud *raspberry*.

senses.gloss: What a person feels, says, or does in answer to something that happens.
examples: His first *reaction* was to laugh.
The mayor's *reaction* to the report was cautious.
We filmed people's *reactions* to the surprise.

senses.gloss: A harmful physical response of the body to a food, drug, or other substance.
examples: She had a *reaction* to the antibiotic and broke out in hives.
Peanuts can cause a severe *reaction* in some kids.
Serious *reactions* to the shot are rare.

senses.gloss: The achieving of something that was planned, hoped for, or imagined.
examples: Opening the bakery was the *realization* of a lifelong dream.
The park is the *realization* of an idea he had thirty years ago.
Full *realization* of the plan will take another decade.

senses.gloss: A football player whose job is to catch passes thrown down the field.
examples: The *receiver* caught the ball in the end zone.
They drafted a fast *receiver* out of Alabama.
Two of their best *receivers* are out with injuries.

senses.gloss: The getting back of something that was lost, stolen, or damaged.
examples: The *recovery* of the stolen paintings took years.
Divers helped with the *recovery* of the wreckage.
He paid a shop for data *recovery* after the drive failed.

senses.gloss: The exchanging of a coupon, gift card, or points for goods, cash, or a service.
senses.ru: погашение купона, обмен баллов на товар
examples: The coupon lists a *redemption* deadline of March 1.
Points *redemption* starts at ten thousand miles.
The store tracks *redemption* of its gift cards.

senses.gloss: A thick, concentrated sauce made by boiling a liquid down.
examples: The steak came with a red wine *reduction*.
Simmer the vinegar until it turns into a syrupy *reduction*.
He drizzled a balsamic *reduction* over the strawberries.

senses.gloss: The official document showing that a vehicle is legally recorded with the state.
examples: The officer asked for my license and *registration*.
My *registration* expires at the end of the month.
Keep the *registration* in the glove compartment.

senses.gloss: An official list or record kept by a government or organization.
examples: His name showed up on the state sex offender *registry*.
She signed up for the national bone marrow *registry*.
County *registries* hold every deed going back a century.

senses.gloss: The controlling of an activity or process by rules or by a system.
examples: The bill calls for tighter *regulation* of online lenders.
Sweating helps with the *regulation* of body temperature.
The industry has resisted *regulation* for decades.

senses.gloss: A government agency or official that oversees an industry and enforces its rules.
examples: Federal *regulators* opened an investigation into the bank.
The company must satisfy the *regulator* before the merger closes.
State *regulators* fined the utility ten million dollars.

senses.gloss: A connection or link between two things, facts, or numbers.
examples: The study found a clear *relationship* between sleep and grades.
There is no *relationship* between the two events.
Economists argue about the *relationship* of wages to inflation.

senses.gloss: The easing or loosening of a rule, limit, or restriction.
examples: Businesses welcomed the *relaxation* of the mask rules.
A slight *relaxation* of lending standards followed the vote.
The *relaxation* of travel limits came too late for summer.

senses.gloss: A person who acts, speaks, or sells on behalf of a company or group.
examples: A customer service *representative* will be with you shortly.
She works as a pharmaceutical sales *representative*.
Union *representatives* met with management on Friday.

senses.gloss: A feeling of doubt that keeps you from fully agreeing or approving.
examples: I have serious *reservations* about hiring him.
She accepted the offer without *reservation*.
His only *reservation* was the price.

senses.gloss: An area of land in the United States set aside for a Native American tribe.
examples: He grew up on a *reservation* in South Dakota.
The tribe runs a health clinic on the *reservation*.
Several *reservations* border the national forest.

senses.gloss: A large supply of something that can be drawn on when needed.
examples: The mayor still has a deep *reservoir* of goodwill in the city.
The country has a huge *reservoir* of untapped talent.
Years of teaching gave her a *reservoir* of patience.

senses.gloss: A container inside a machine that holds liquid until it is needed.
examples: Fill the *reservoir* with cold water before you brew the coffee.
The windshield washer *reservoir* is empty again.
Both *reservoirs* on the humidifier need cleaning.

senses.gloss: A doctor who is training in a hospital after finishing medical school.
examples: A first-year *resident* stitched up the cut.
The *resident* on call paged the attending physician.
*Residents* often work thirty-hour shifts.

senses.gloss: Quiet acceptance of something unpleasant that cannot be changed.
examples: He shrugged with *resignation* and picked up the mop.
There was *resignation* in her voice when she finally agreed.
The crowd waited in tired *resignation*.

senses.gloss: A firm decision to do or stop doing something.
examples: My New Year's *resolution* is to run three times a week.
She made a *resolution* to call her parents every Sunday.
Most *resolutions* are broken by February.

senses.gloss: The solving or settling of a problem, argument, or difficult situation.
examples: Both sides say they want a peaceful *resolution*.
The case dragged on for years without *resolution*.
The company pays for conflict *resolution* training.

senses.gloss: A formal statement that a group votes on and adopts.
examples: The city council passed a *resolution* honoring the firefighters.
The U.N. *resolution* demanded an immediate ceasefire.
Two *resolutions* failed by a single vote.

senses.gloss: A machine that breathes for a patient who cannot breathe alone.
examples: He spent two weeks on a *respirator* after the accident.
The hospital ran short of *respirators* during the surge.
Doctors took her off the *respirator* on Sunday.

senses.gloss: The bringing back of something that had stopped or been taken away.
examples: Crews promised full *restoration* of power by midnight.
The treaty led to the *restoration* of diplomatic ties.
Voters approved the *restoration* of the library's funding.

senses.gloss: A strap, belt, or device that holds a person or animal in place.
examples: Every child under eight needs a proper car *restraint*.
The nurse loosened the *restraints* on his wrists.
The roller coaster's shoulder *restraints* lock automatically.
